title: V8 (JavaScript engine)
summary: V8 is Google's open-source JavaScript and WebAssembly engine, first released with Chrome in 2008. It compiles ECMAScript to native machine code using a multi-tiered JIT pipeline. The engine has evolved from Crankshaft to TurboFan, with Ignition as the baseline interpreter. A recent tiered system adds SparkPlug and Maglev to optimize code based on execution frequency, targeting both performance and low-memory devices like Android phones.

mechanisms.title: Baseline Interpreter (Ignition)
mechanisms.explanation: Ignition is a register-based bytecode interpreter that parses ECMAScript into V8's internal bytecode format. It was introduced to reduce memory usage on small-memory devices compared to earlier optimizing compilers. It generates bytecode from the abstract syntax tree, which TurboFan later compiles into machine code.

mechanisms.title: Optimizing Compiler (TurboFan)
mechanisms.explanation: TurboFan is V8's optimizing just-in-time compiler. It compiles bytecode into native machine code and performs dynamic optimizations at runtime based on execution profiles. Techniques include inlining, elision of expensive runtime properties, and inline caching. It handles challenging workloads such as asm.js and is part of the main compiler pipeline alongside Ignition.
